title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
gist: NgRx 22 adds an experimental @ngrx/signals/resource entry point with resource extensions that patch Angular's resource/httpResource behaviour (value reset to undefined on reload, throwing in error state) while preserving the original type, plus dynamic deep signals for union-typed state and a SignalStoreFeatureType helper. Upgrading requires Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0, and community comments suggest signal-based state is cutting Angular boilerplate and the need for RxJS and NgRx.

themes.theme: Resource extensions for Angular's resource API

insights.claim: NgRx 22 ships resource extensions in a new experimental @ngrx/signals/resource entry point. They wrap Angular's resource and httpResource, which otherwise reset value() to undefined while reloading and throw when read in an error state, and they patch only those behaviours while preserving the original resource type.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The state-management layer is filling gaps in Angular's own resource primitives, which shows where the core framework API is still immature.
insights.quote: Resource extensions wrap an existing resource and patch only those behaviours, while preserving the original resource type.
insights.locator: The main new addition is resource extensions

insights.claim: NgRx 22 includes four built-in resource extensions and a provideResourceExtensions function that registers default extensions at the application, route or component level.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Teams can set resource behaviour centrally across an Angular app instead of wrapping each call site.

insights.claim: NgRx maintainer Marko Stanimirović argued that changing Angular resource error behaviour is a prerequisite for deeper SignalStore integration, because once a resource is in the error state any later patchState call throws, since patchState reads value() internally.
insights.speaker: Marko Stanimirović
insights.so_what: Throwing error semantics in Angular resources directly block store integration, so this fix unlocks NgRx's planned SignalStore roadmap.
insights.quote: once a resource enters the error state, any subsequent patchState call will throw because it reads value() internally

insights.claim: A community roundup on DEV said similar behaviour could be built with Angular's snapshot() plus extra state logic, but resource extensions let developers stay on the resource itself, keeping the value writable and keeping the more specific httpResource type.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The value of the feature is ergonomics and type preservation rather than new capability.
insights.quote: with Resource Extensions, you stay on the resource itself
insights.locator: A community roundup on DEV noted

insights.claim: Competing Angular tools already offer similar behaviour: TanStack Query for Angular keeps previous data when query keys change through placeholderData: keepPreviousData, and the community NgRx Toolkit's withResource has supported a non-throwing undefined value, previous-value and error-handling strategies for SignalStore since v20.6.0.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: NgRx is catching up to features that rival and community libraries shipped first, so the Angular state-management market stays contested.
insights.locator: TanStack Query for Angular offers similar

insights.claim: Commenters on the NgRx resource-extensions RFC were positive: Manfred Steyer replied "Love it!" and suggested an activation signal, and another commenter asked for parity with SolidJS's createResource, such as access to the current value inside the loader.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Community requests point to SolidJS's resource model as the reference design for Angular's signal-based data loading.

themes.theme: SignalStore typing and dynamic deep signals

insights.claim: In NgRx 22, deep signals are dynamic: a state slice typed as a union, the usual way to model "not loaded yet", used to collapse into a single flat Signal, but now each object-literal member gets its own DeepSignal, reachable after narrowing with an in check.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Union-typed loading states can now be modelled in SignalStore without losing fine-grained reactivity.
insights.locator: Version 22 also makes deep signals dynamic

insights.claim: NgRx 22 adds a SignalStoreFeatureType utility that extracts the state and members of a feature factory, so custom SignalStore features can reuse them as input types instead of redeclaring them by hand.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: This reduces typing boilerplate for teams that build reusable SignalStore features.

insights.claim: In NgRx 22, @ngrx/store-devtools gains an actionCreators option for dispatching actions from Redux DevTools, and @ngrx/eslint-plugin supports ESLint v10 while dropping ESLint v8 and the legacy .eslintrc format.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Projects still on ESLint v8 or .eslintrc must migrate their lint config before adopting NgRx 22 tooling.

themes.theme: Upgrade requirements and Angular 22 timing changes

insights.claim: Upgrading to NgRx 22 requires Angular 22, TypeScript 6.0 and RxJS ^6.5 or ^7.5. The upgrade runs via ng update @ngrx/store@22, or ng update @ngrx/signals@22 for SignalStore-only projects, and most breaking changes have automated migrations.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: NgRx adoption is tied to the Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0 upgrade cycle, which sets the pace for enterprise migration work.

insights.claim: Angular 22 changed resource timing. One developer reported test failures from the change, and it was later added to Angular's release notes as a breaking change.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: This is a hidden upgrade cost: test suites that depend on resource timing may break during Angular 22 migrations.
insights.locator: Teams should also note that Angular 22

insights.claim: A Hacker News user said NgRx Signals cuts state setup from about five files to usually one, with all or most functionality co-located.
insights.speaker: Hacker News user
insights.so_what: Lower boilerplate is the main adoption driver for signal-based state management in Angular.
insights.quote: Instead of having 5 files to get state hooked up, its usually 1 file and all/most functionality is co-located.
insights.locator: In the Hacker News thread for Angular v22

insights.claim: Another Hacker News user said modern Angular needs far less boilerplate than the v2 and v4 days, and that RxJS and NgRx are becoming less and less necessary.
insights.speaker: Hacker News user
insights.so_what: As built-in Angular signals mature, NgRx's role may shrink, which is a long-term relevance risk for NgRx and RxJS.
insights.quote: And even RxJS and NgRX are becoming less and less necessary to use too, which is great.

insights.claim: NgRx is an open-source, community-driven Angular framework that provides global state management with Store and Effects alongside the signal-based SignalStore, and it is sponsored by Nx and CodeRabbit.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Developer-tool vendors such as Nx and CodeRabbit fund the infrastructure of the Angular ecosystem.
insights.locator: NgRx is an open-source, community-driven framework
